headline_marked: [[2 Bangladeshis killed]] in Saudi airport attacks; flights suspended
headline: 2 Bangladeshis killed in Saudi airport attacks; flights suspended
summary: Biman Bangladesh Airlines suspends flights to Riyadh and Dammam until Sunday due to ongoing Houthi rebel attacks on Saudi airports. Two Bangladeshis were among 13 killed in a recent Riyadh airport assault.
details: Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended its flights from Dhaka to Dammam and Riyadh until Sunday, citing passenger safety amid ongoing attacks on Saudi airports. The airline stated that further decisions and updated travel schedules will be announced soon. Passengers with urgent travel needs can still use Jeddah and Madinah international airports.

To accommodate passenger demand, Biman has deployed larger Boeing 777 aircraft on the Madinah route, increasing capacity by 148 seats per flight, and added three extra flights on the Jeddah route. Passengers are advised to contact Biman sales centres for inquiries. Meanwhile, US-Bangla Airlines has cancelled all flights on the Dhaka-Riyadh route until October 21.

A total of 103 flights from Dhaka have been cancelled or suspended as operations at Riyadh and Dammam airports were halted due to attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels. These include 42 direct flights and 61 transit flights. Among the direct flights, Biman cancelled 17, US-Bangla 10, Saudia eight, and Riyadh Air seven.

Yemeni Houthi forces have repeatedly targeted Saudi airports since last Saturday. An attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport resulted in 13 foreign nationals killed and 308 injured. Two Bangladeshi nationals were among the deceased, with 27 others sustaining injuries.

The Houthis, who are backed by Iran, vowed on Wednesday to conduct further strikes against Saudi airports and oil facilities, following an attack on Saudi Aramco headquarters. They frame these strikes as retaliation for Saudi military operations in Yemen. The escalating conflict raises fears of wider regional instability.
